respiratory-sinus-arrhythmia.short: The heart speeds up as you breathe in and slows as you breathe out, because the vagus brake eases and returns with each breath. It is the main source of short-term HRV at rest.

sdnn.short: Standard deviation of the beat-to-beat intervals, in ms: how widely RR intervals spread around their average over the recording. It ignores the order of the beats.

time-domain-hrv.short: HRV measures worked out straight from the series of RR intervals, in milliseconds. RMSSD and SDNN are time-domain measures.

frequency-domain-hrv.short: HRV measures that sort the up-and-down swings of the RR intervals by how fast they repeat (cycles per second, Hz) and report how much of the variation falls in each band, such as LF and HF.

hf-power.short: The part of HRV that swings 0.15–0.40 times per second, the range of normal breathing. At rest, with normal breathing, it mostly reflects the vagus acting through RSA.

lf-power.short: The part of HRV that swings 0.04–0.15 times per second (one swing every 7–25 s). It mixes vagal and sympathetic influences, so it is not a clean sympathetic measure.

ppg.short: Reading the pulse with light: a sensor on the skin tracks the blood volume changes with each beat. Phone cameras and the optical sensors in watches and rings work this way.

rolling-mean.short: An average of the last N days that moves forward each day: a 7-day rolling mean drops the oldest day and adds today's. It smooths out day-to-day noise.

hrv-guided-training.short: Choosing each day's session from that morning's HRV compared with your own recent range: a hard day if HRV is normal or up, an easy day or rest if it has dropped.

predefined-training.short: A plan fixed in advance, with the hard and easy days set before the block starts, whatever the daily readings or feelings turn out to be.

hrv-saturation.short: At very high vagal activity (a low resting HR), vagal HRV indices stop rising and can even fall. A lower HRV then does not mean less vagal activity or more fatigue.

readiness-score.short: A single daily number from an app or wearable (often 0–100) that blends HRV, resting heart rate, sleep and sometimes training load. The formula is usually not published.

ecg.short: A recording of the heart's electrical signal from sensors on the skin. It times each beat exactly, so it is the reference that other HRV devices are checked against.
